name: PSLE Singapore Oral Practice Rubric - Moderately Strict
subject: English
description: Upload-ready PSLE-style Singapore English Oral practice rubric for reading aloud and stimulus-based conversation. This is a structured practice rubric, not an official SEAB marking scheme.

criteria.name: Reading Aloud - Pronunciation
criteria.description: Reading aloud pronunciation: assesses accurate pronunciation of words, clear articulation, and beginning and ending sounds. Score conservatively if the transcript or audio evidence is unclear.

rubric_levels.description: Pronounces almost all words accurately and clearly, including beginning and ending sounds. Errors, if any, do not affect meaning.
Pronounces most words clearly with a few minor errors. Beginning and ending sounds are usually clear.
Pronunciation is understandable but several words or word endings are unclear or inaccurate.
Frequent pronunciation errors make parts of the reading difficult to understand.
Very unclear pronunciation or very little usable reading evidence.
No reading attempt or no usable audio/transcript evidence.

criteria.name: Reading Aloud - Expression
criteria.description: Reading aloud expression: assesses pitch, tone, phrasing, and awareness of meaning, purpose, audience, and context.

rubric_levels.description: Reads with suitable expression, tone, phrasing, and awareness of meaning throughout.
Uses appropriate tone and phrasing most of the time, with occasional flat or unnatural parts.
Shows some expression, but tone or phrasing is uneven and meaning is not always well conveyed.
Reads with little variation in pitch or tone; expression is mostly flat or mechanical.
Very limited expression or too little usable reading evidence.
No reading attempt or no usable audio/transcript evidence.

criteria.name: Reading Aloud - Delivery and Fluency
criteria.description: Reading aloud delivery and fluency: assesses smoothness, pace, pauses, hesitation, and continuity while reading the passage.

rubric_levels.description: Reads smoothly with suitable pace, natural pauses, and very little hesitation.
Reads mostly smoothly with appropriate pace and pauses, though there may be minor hesitation.
Reading is understandable but pace, pauses, or hesitation are uneven.
Reading is slow, jerky, or frequently interrupted by awkward pauses and hesitation.
Very halting reading or too little usable reading evidence.
No reading attempt or no usable audio/transcript evidence.

criteria.name: Stimulus Response Relevance
criteria.description: Stimulus-based conversation: assesses whether the student answers the question directly, refers accurately to the picture stimulus, and gives a relevant personal or thoughtful response.

rubric_levels.description: Answers the question directly with accurate and specific reference to the picture, plus a clear personal or thoughtful response.
Mostly answers the question and makes some relevant reference to the picture, but details may be general.
Partly answers the question, but picture reference is weak, vague, or not well connected.
Response is mostly generic, only loosely related to the picture or question.
No meaningful answer, or answer is unrelated to the question and picture.

criteria.name: Idea Development
criteria.description: Stimulus-based conversation: assesses elaboration, reasons, examples, explanation, and ability to extend beyond a short or surface-level answer.

rubric_levels.description: Develops ideas clearly with relevant reasons, examples, explanation, and thoughtful extension.
Gives clear ideas with at least one useful reason or example, but development could be richer.
Gives a basic idea with limited explanation, examples, or reasoning.
Very brief answer with little elaboration or unclear reasoning.
No developed idea.

criteria.name: Spoken Language Use
criteria.description: Stimulus-based conversation: assesses grammar, sentence control, vocabulary, clarity, and suitability of spoken English for a Primary 6 oral response.

rubric_levels.description: Uses accurate, varied sentence structures and suitable vocabulary. Meaning is clear and natural.
Uses mostly accurate language with appropriate vocabulary. Minor errors do not affect meaning.
Uses simple but understandable language. Noticeable grammar or sentence errors are present.
Frequent language errors, limited vocabulary, or incomplete sentences affect clarity.
Very limited spoken language evidence.
No usable spoken response.

criteria.name: Interaction and Confidence
criteria.description: Stimulus-based conversation: assesses confidence, willingness to continue, responsiveness to prompts, and ability to build on a guiding question if one is given.

rubric_levels.description: Responds confidently, stays engaged, and builds naturally on the question or guiding prompt.
Responds adequately with some confidence, though support or prompting may be needed.
Gives a hesitant, very brief, or dependent response that needs substantial support.
No meaningful interaction or response.
